claims.statement: Bremelanotide, marketed as Vyleesi, is FDA-approved as a melanocortin receptor agonist indicated for the treatment of premenopausal women with acquired, generalized hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD); the label explicitly states it is not indicated for HSDD in postmenopausal women or in men, and not indicated to enhance sexual performance.

context.population: premenopausal women with acquired, generalized HSDD

extractedEvidence.quote: VYLEESI is a melanocortin receptor agonist indicated for the treatment of premenopausal women with acquired, generalized hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD)
Not indicated for treatment of HSDD in postmenopausal women or in men
Not indicated to enhance sexual performance

reviewFlags: safety-critical/regulatory claim; confirm current label version against live DailyMed setid at review time

claims.statement: Vyleesi is contraindicated in patients with uncontrolled hypertension or known cardiovascular disease, and the label warns that bremelanotide causes a transient increase in blood pressure and decrease in heart rate after each dose that usually resolves within 12 hours.

context.population: patients with uncontrolled hypertension or known cardiovascular disease

extractedEvidence.quote: Uncontrolled hypertension or known cardiovascular disease
Transient increase in blood pressure and decrease in heart rate: Occurs after each dose and usually resolves within 12 hours

claims.statement: In FDA-approved labeling, nausea was reported by 40% of patients receiving up to 8 monthly doses of Vyleesi, requiring anti-emetic therapy in 13% of patients; focal hyperpigmentation (face, gingiva, breasts) was reported by 1% of patients receiving up to 8 doses per month. The RECONNECT phase 3 trials separately reported nausea, flushing, and headache each occurring in 10% or more of bremelanotide-treated patients versus placebo, mostly mild to moderate in intensity.

context.population: premenopausal women with HSDD treated in clinical trials and post-approval labeling review
context.doseText: up to 8 doses per month (label-reported exposure, not a use recommendation)

extractedEvidence.quote: Nausea: Reported by 40% of patients who received up to 8 monthly doses, requiring anti-emetic therapy in 13% of patients
Focal hyperpigmentation: Reported by 1% of patients who received up to 8 doses per month, including involvement of the face, gingiva and breasts
Patients taking bremelanotide experienced more nausea, flushing, and headache (10% or more in both studies) compared with placebo.

reviewFlags: focal hyperpigmentation may be irreversible in some cases per label context; confirm reversibility language at review

claims.statement: Bremelanotide is a synthetic cyclic heptapeptide melanocortin receptor agonist (active metabolite of the earlier candidate melanotan II) that acts on melanocortin receptors, including MC4R, implicated in central regulation of sexual arousal/desire pathways.

extractedEvidence.quote: VYLEESI is a melanocortin receptor agonist indicated for the treatment of premenopausal women with acquired, generalized hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD)

reviewFlags: DrugBank mechanism-of-action page did not fully render in this session; verify receptor-subtype specificity (MC4R vs other melanocortin receptors) against a primary pharmacology source at review time

claims.statement: In two identical phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials (RECONNECT; total 1,267 premenopausal women with HSDD randomized, 1,202 in the efficacy population), as-needed subcutaneous bremelanotide 1.75 mg over 24 weeks produced statistically significant improvements versus placebo on both co-primary endpoints: increase in Female Sexual Function Index-desire domain score (Study 301: +0.30, P<.001; Study 302: +0.42, P<.001) and reduction in Female Sexual Distress Scale-Desire/Arousal/Orgasm score (Study 301: -0.37, P<.001; Study 302: -0.29, P=.005).

context.population: premenopausal women with acquired, generalized HSDD (n=1,267 randomized)
context.doseText: 1.75 mg subcutaneously as needed, over a 24-week trial period (trial protocol description; not a use recommendation)

extractedEvidence.quote: Female Sexual Function Index-desire domain: Bremelanotide showed statistically significant increases compared to placebo across both studies (Study 301: 0.30, P<.001; Study 302: 0.42, P<.001; integrated: 0.35, P<.001)
Female Sexual Distress Scale: Significant reductions in distress (Study 301: -0.37, P<.001; Study 302: -0.29, P=.005; integrated: -0.33, P<.001)

reviewFlags: effect sizes are modest on validated instrument scales; clinical-meaningfulness interpretation should not be overstated

claims.statement: Only the FDA-approved subcutaneous autoinjector form (Vyleesi, 1.75 mg) has controlled human efficacy and safety data supporting the HSDD indication. Compounded PT-141 nasal spray products sold online (commonly 1-2 mg per spray, per vendor marketing) are not FDA-approved formulations and are not supported by the RECONNECT trial evidence, which tested only the subcutaneous route; a vendor page explicitly frames intranasal PT-141 as 'off-label' even while acknowledging Vyleesi's approval status.

context.population: consumers/patients seeking PT-141 outside the approved indication or route
context.formulation: compounded PT-141 nasal spray, various vendor concentrations
context.useCase: off-label/unapproved-formulation use marketed for libido or general sexual enhancement

extractedEvidence.quote: PT-141 (bremelanotide) is FDA-approved as Vyleesi for premenopausal women with HSDD. Compounded intranasal use is off-label and requires a prescription.
Compounded intranasal PT-141 is commonly prepared at 1 mg to 2 mg per spray
VYLEESI is a melanocortin receptor agonist indicated for the treatment of premenopausal women with acquired, generalized hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD)

reviewFlags: misinformation-adjacent: vendor marketing extrapolates an approved subcutaneous product's evidence to an unapproved intranasal route and broader 'sexual enhancement' framing not supported by the label, which explicitly excludes performance-enhancement use
no controlled human trial for intranasal PT-141 was located in this session; confirm absence/presence at independent review
